questions.stem: Which statement correctly describes a key difference between xerophyte and hydrophyte leaf adaptations?

options.text: Xerophytes have thin cuticles while hydrophytes have thick cuticles
Xerophytes have adaptations to reduce water loss while hydrophytes have adaptations to promote gas exchange underwater
Xerophytes have more stomata than hydrophytes
Hydrophytes have deeper roots than xerophytes

questions.explanation: Xerophytes live in dry conditions and have adaptations such as thick cuticles, sunken stomata, and rolled leaves to minimise water loss. Hydrophytes live in water and have adaptations such as aerenchyma and stomata on the upper leaf surface to facilitate gas exchange in aquatic environments.
